chapter: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
title: Knocking on doors for rooms on Claude's southern tour
summary: Touring Birmingham and the South with Hopkins, the band had to find lodging by asking strangers for directions to rooms, often finding hotels full.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: This period that you were with Claud Hopkins, was that all just one tour? You went out to West Virginia, back, and --

Naw, it wasn't -- naw, heck no. I mean we went -- we went -- oh, we did -- later on we went farther than that. I'm trying to think how far south did we go, or when or where. We had a girl singer. Yeah, because we -- I remember Birmingham, Alabama.
-- with Claude in the south, and in places like Alabama?

It seemed rough, because at that time we had to go knock on doors, and say pardon me, Madam, would you, or do you happen to have a room that you would like to or care to rent? I'm here with the band, such and such a band, we're going to be here two nights, three nights, and need a place to stay. Yes, or no?

No, but -- I say well do you know of some place, and they say well go down the street by the old oak tree and make a left and turn, and don't go in there, because that's a -- they, you know, that -- how you get those directions, and you finally -- you hope -- find some place, you know.
But you have to go all over town yourself looking for them?

Weren't there -- after -- if you're playing some place in Birmingham, let's say, there had been other bands that had come through and played, and after that had gone on for a while, well weren't there certain places that became established to live --
Yes, if you knew where to start asking.
But didn't the people who ran the ballroom, or wherever you were going to play --

Well there were -- they would -- you'd run into anybody in the street, and say know where I can get a room, fellow? Yes. Why don't you go down to Mrs. So-and-so's, or they'd figure you know. Yeah, but where is that? Which direction? Oh, well you go down here, then turn, and turn, and -- they'd direct you that way.

And in Birmingham they had a little shanty there, little thing they called a hotel, and it's -- oh, well we're having a convention, in town, church convention, or something, and we're all filled up, you know, maybe, you know. I mean that -- well you had -- you ran into that even in the biggest hotels, sometimes. You get into town and there's some kind of convention, and it's full. I mean, so
that's different. And maybe you get -- well, if you keep looking, had plenty of time to spend, you -- usually you would find something, here, there, and with --
